concepts.learning_objective: Explain what a variable, an observation and data are, using the example of food grain production.
State the purpose of collecting data in economics.

topics.title: Sources of data: primary and secondary

concepts.learning_objective: Identify primary data as first-hand information collected by the investigator through an enquiry.
Identify secondary data as data collected and processed by another agency and state its advantages.
Apply the rules for framing good questions: brief, clear, general to specific, no leading or double-negative questions.
Distinguish open-ended questions from closed-ended two-way and multiple-choice questions, with their merits and limits.

topics.title: Modes of data collection and pilot survey

concepts.learning_objective: Compare personal interviews, mailed questionnaires and telephone interviews by their merits and demerits.
Explain the purpose of a pilot survey (pre-testing of the questionnaire).
Describe the census or complete enumeration method and the Indian Census.
Identify the population and a representative sample for a given study and state why sample surveys are preferred.
Explain random sampling, the lottery method and random number tables.
Explain non-random sampling based on judgement, purpose, convenience or quota.
Calculate the sampling error as the difference between a population parameter and its sample estimate.
Identify non-sampling errors (sampling bias, non-response, errors in data acquisition) and explain why they are more serious.
State the main facts about the Census of India as a source of demographic data.
Describe the role of the National Sample Survey and its publication Sarvekshana.
